transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, what brings me in is... I keep having these strange moments lately. My own house, or even my office, just feels completely unreal sometimes. It's hard to explain, but it's almost like I'm watching myself from across the room instead of actually being there. It keeps happening, so I figured I needed to come see someone about it.
How long have you been experiencing these strange, unreal moments?
It's been about two weeks now. It started right after... well, I had a client actually threaten me right there in my office. Ever since that happened, I've been getting these moments.
Have you been feeling anxious or on edge since the incident with your client?

Yeah, I have. Very much on edge. Even when I'm just at home in Roanoke, I keep tracking every little sound. If I hear a car door shut outside, or a footstep on the porch, my attention just snaps right to it. And wherever I am, I'm always checking where the exits are... it's like I just feel this need to be ready, you know, in case someone tries to come at me again.
Have you experienced hearing or seeing things that aren't there since the incident with your client?

No, no, I haven't had anything like that. I mean, I pay way too much attention to real sounds, like I was just saying, but I'm not hearing voices or seeing things that aren't actually there. It's really just the actual things around me that put me on edge.
Do you feel like you're disconnected from yourself or your body during these unreal moments?

Yeah, that's exactly it. That's actually the main thing that made me realize I needed to come in and talk to someone. I keep having these moments where my own house, or my office, just feels completely unreal. And when it happens, it's like... well, it's like I'm watching myself from across the room instead of actually being there in my own body.
Have you been experiencing any physical symptoms like headaches or stomach problems since the incident with your client?

No, not really. I mean... physically, I feel fine. My stomach hasn't been bothering me, and I haven't had any headaches. It's really just the mental side of things, like being so on edge and having those weird out-of-body moments I mentioned. But physically, no, I haven't noticed any issues like that.
Have you been avoiding any places or activities since the incident with your client?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I still go to work, I still go to the grocery store... I haven't really stopped doing anything or avoided any specific places. I'm just more on edge when I'm there, but I'm not avoiding them.
Have you been feeling less emotionally responsive or disconnected from your feelings since the incident with your client?

Yeah, I have actually. It's... well, my wife tries to joke with me, or she brings up going fishing like we had planned to do. And I know those things should feel good, or make me happy, but I just don't feel it. It's like the part of me that enjoys them has just been switched off.
Has your ability to function at work or in your daily life been significantly impacted by these feelings of being on edge and disconnected?

Yeah, it has. I've actually missed a few client deadlines recently, which isn't like me at all. And... I've stopped seeing people at the office. I just don't trust myself to handle their tax returns properly right now, or even to keep the workplace safe. It's just too much.
Are there any specific situations or reminders of the incident with your client that you've been trying to avoid?

No, not really. Like I said before, I haven't been avoiding any places. And I'm not really avoiding any specific situations or reminders either. I mean, I'm still doing my work... mostly. I just don't want to see clients in person right now. But it's not because I'm avoiding reminders of what happened, it's just... I don't feel capable right now.
Have you noticed any changes in your relationships with family or friends since you started feeling this way?

I wouldn't say there have been any big changes, no. I mean, my wife has noticed I'm not really reacting to things the way I used to, like I mentioned before with the jokes and the fishing trip. But other than that... I haven't really noticed anything different with my friends or family. I'm just kind of going through the motions, I guess.
Have you been feeling distant or disconnected from your loved ones since these strange moments started happening?

Not really distant, no. I mean, I'm still spending time with my wife, and I still talk to my friends when they call. It's not like I'm pushing anyone away or feeling cut off from them. It's just... like I was saying, I'm just kind of flat right now. My reactions aren't really there, but the connection with them hasn't changed.
Have you experienced any memory gaps or difficulty recalling specific details about the incident with your client or the time since then?

Yeah, actually, there is a piece missing. I remember him crowding me in my office, and I remember the police being there later. But the middle part... like, exactly what he said right before I reached for the phone... it's just a blank. No matter how hard I try to pull it up, I just can't remember that specific part.
Have you been avoiding talking or thinking about the incident with your client?

No, not really. I mean, I don't go out of my way to bring it up, but if someone asks, I'll tell them what happened. And I definitely still think about it. It just kind of pops into my head sometimes, especially when I'm at work. So, no, I wouldn't say I'm avoiding it.
Have you forgotten any other events or periods of time since the incident with your client, beyond just the part where you can't remember what he said?

No, I don't think so. Everything else since then has been pretty clear. I remember the rest of that day, and my memory for everything else over the last little while has been perfectly normal. It's really just that one specific blank spot during the actual incident. I haven't noticed any other missing time.
Do you feel guilty or ashamed about what happened with your client or how you've been feeling since then?

No, I don't feel guilty. I mean, I didn't do anything wrong. I was just doing my job, and he was the one who got aggressive. And as for how I've been feeling... I guess it's just a normal reaction to something like that happening. I don't feel ashamed of it. It's just something I have to deal with.
Have you experienced any other memory gaps or difficulty recalling specific details about events since the incident with your client?
No, I haven't. Like I said just a minute ago, my memory's been fine other than that one blank spot during the incident itself. Everything else has been clear.
Are there any activities or situations that you've been avoiding because they remind you of the incident with your client?

No, not really. I mean, I still go into the office every day and do my regular routine. I can't think of any specific places or activities I'm staying away from. I'm just going about my business as usual, really.
